summary: A concise overview of this week's technology developments, focusing on advancements in artificial intelligence, digital engineering, and cloud infrastructure challenges.

items.title: Anthropic is hiring an AI chip design team
items.summary: Anthropic is building a dedicated team to design its own custom AI chips. This co-design of hardware and models aims to make the company's Claude-powered technology run faster and more efficiently.

items.title: MacPaw taps Liquid AI to offer on-device inference to devs building for its app store
items.summary: MacPaw is partnering with Liquid AI to provide on-device AI inference capabilities for developers on its app store. The collaboration will also power a local version of MacPaw's AI assistant, Eney.

items.title: Texas halts data center connections to power grid amid overwhelming demand
items.summary: Texas has paused new data center connections to its power grid due to overwhelming demand. This decision highlights the growing infrastructure challenges posed by the rapid expansion of AI technologies.

items.title: Trump’s AI testing plan is limited and vague
items.summary: The Trump administration has released a voluntary framework for assessing cybersecurity risks in advanced AI models. However, the guidelines have faced criticism for being vague and completely excluding open-source models from testing.

items.title: 2027 Chevrolet Corvette Grand Sport X proves code is as important as hardware
items.summary: Chevrolet's new 721-horsepower hybrid Corvette demonstrates how software code has become as critical as physical hardware in modern automotive design. The vehicle showcases the growing intersection of digital engineering and traditional manufacturing.
